Old transport classified these as definite failures/cancellation.

contract.stdio: Mark possible delivery immediately after successful StreamWriter.write(), before drain. BrokenPipe/Reset after that boundary, drain cancellation and existing timeout/response-loss cases raise MCPUncertain for tools/call, while initial write raising before successful return stays not sent. Reclaim remains original5s/ownership flow; no retransmission.
contract.http: Waiting for stream context entry is waiting for response headers, not proof that no outgoing request left. Read/write/protocol/close failures or cancellation after handing off a tools/call are conservatively MCPUncertain even without headers. Before any response, ConnectError/ConnectTimeout/PoolTimeout retain documented no-send classification; after a response even such an exception is uncertain. Authorization/header preparation and before_send remain before the handoff exception scope. Known401/403/other4xx and discovery/handshake contracts unchanged.
contract.uncertainty: sent=true means a request may have left, not proof that a remote operation succeeded. Missing headers never prove nonexecution. Actual complete server receipt is independently demonstrated only in the native loopback tests; injected exceptions only validate failure classification.
contract.business: Two isolated real SQLite/HTTP/model-scripted write flows require owner approval before any file write. Local MCP fixture appends once then disconnects or sends an invalid status line. mcp_calls and action persist unknown/Effect.UNKNOWN; owner inspection records applied without rewriting original unknown outcome. Same turn key remains duplicate and no additional tools/call occurs.
contract.unchanged: No changed transport deadlines, automatic retries, credential gates, authorization bypass, result payload disclosure, schema or public error codes.
